title: FRSB in the SK spin glass: convergence to full-interval support at zero temperature
abstract: We prove full replica symmetry breaking for the zero-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at zero temperature: the Parisi minimizer is absolutely continuous, has a smooth density, and has support $[0,1)$. At inverse temperature $β>1$, [arxiv.org/abs/2607.11756v3] recently proved that the Parisi measure has support $[0,q_β]$. Here, we show $q_β$ converges to $1$ as $β\to\infty$.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model exhibits full replica symmetry breaking at zero temperature. By analyzing the Parisi measure, the authors demonstrate that this measure has continuous support across the entire interval [0, 1). This result provides deep mathematical insight into the low-temperature phase structure of mean-field disordered systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is proving full replica symmetry breaking (FRSB) for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass model at zero temperature.
main_result: The authors prove that at zero temperature, the Parisi measure has full support on the interval [0, 1), and its density function is smooth and non-zero across this entire range.
method: The analysis involves developing variational self-consistency theorems for the Parisi functional, utilizing stochastic processes (Itô's formula), and employing advanced PDE techniques to establish regularity and convergence bounds.

The argument flows from general variational principles to specific PDE stability proofs.
why_interesting: While focused on classical spin glasses, the mathematical machinery involving complex functional analysis, convergence theorems for measures, and solving associated PDEs is highly relevant to understanding quantum many-body systems in disordered or frustrated regimes.
